author: ING Broker editorial team
content:
Employee accident insurance concerns the people included and the consequences of an accident specified in the contract. It is not the same as employer's liability and does not mean payment for every health problem. A Moldovan company should check who is insured, for which activities, during which hours and how benefits are calculated.

The local market publicly presents group accident programmes, for example through GRAWE Moldova. This indicates the category exists, not that particular conditions apply to every workforce. This material explains preparation and comparison. Conditions, individual acceptance and claims decisions must be checked with the insurer in the applicable documents.

Establish the purpose of the staff package

Start by discussing what the company wants: a workforce benefit, financial protection for specified consequences of an accident or an addition to an existing programme. Do not begin solely with the budget. A clear objective helps select people, periods and the questions that need asking.

Separate insurance from workplace prevention. A policy does not replace training, protective equipment or technical checks. Employer legal duties require a distinct assessment by competent specialists. This article does not equate voluntary insurance with fulfilment of those duties.

Describe the actual occupation, not just a job title

An “operator” may work at a desk, at machinery or in the field. Prepare a short description of usual duties and occasional activities. Include travel, work at height or particular equipment only where these form part of the person's actual role.

If the workforce has different professions, group them clearly for assessment. Do not conceal differing exposures under one administrative title. Ask how the contract is updated when an employee changes occupation. The answer should relate to the proposed product rather than an assumed general rule.

Check who can be included

State whether permanent employees, seasonal workers or other categories are being considered. Ask for eligibility criteria and identification arrangements. A connection to the business does not automatically include every collaborator, visitor or subcontractor.

Initially prepare headcounts and occupation categories. Named lists and personal documents should follow only when necessary through an appropriate channel. Avoid sending medical information or identity copies through public forms. The company contact should know who receives information and for what purpose.

Working hours and personal time are different

Ask exactly when protection operates: only during a work-related interval or outside it as well, depending on the offered option. Ask about commuting, business trips and work at another location. Do not infer the answer from the general phrase “employee insurance”.

For shift work, explain the actual schedule. Where activities occur abroad, describe countries and duties before accepting a proposal. Check contractual territory and period separately. Do not automatically import a condition from another group programme's presentation.

Separate risks and amounts for each person

Ask which consequences of an accident qualify for a benefit under the proposed conditions and the amount for each. A benefit is the payment determined under personal insurance conditions. Check whether it is a fixed sum, table-based amount or another contractual calculation.

A large headline amount is not the payment for every accident. Request written examples relevant to the workforce and read applicable limits. Also ask whether a shared limit applies to an event affecting several people. That is a checking question, not a statement of a universal condition.

Do not confuse accident and medical insurance

A medical service package and accident insurance may have different subjects and payment mechanisms. If consultations, investigations or treatment are wanted, explicitly check which product is assessed. Mention of hospitalisation in an accident programme does not establish unlimited medical services.

Likewise, a health problem unrelated to an accident must not be presented as automatically included. Ask for definitions and exclusions, meaning situations without protection. Explain these differences plainly to employees before mistaken expectations arise.

Distinguish employer's liability

Accident cover for a person and a liability claim against the company are different issues. Do not say a benefit payment automatically establishes or removes anyone's liability. The legal position of an event requires a separate review of facts and applicable rules.

When comparing programmes, prepare two question columns: insured people's benefits and company liability risks. If both assessments are needed, say so at the outset. One package name should not hide the absence of confirmation for either component.

Organise employees joining and leaving the programme

Decide who communicates hiring, departures and role changes. Ask for the list update procedure and when an accepted change takes effect. An existing group policy does not mean a new employee is automatically included from their first day.

Keep versions and confirmations. For each change, check people, period and any contractual recalculation. Coordinate seasonal workers with the actual activity calendar without promising retrospective inclusion of people or events.

Keep the employment change date distinct from the confirmed insurance change date in the working record.

Compare cost without losing important conditions

A premium is the amount paid for insurance. Request cost alongside the people, occupations, hours and amounts assessed. Comparison is meaningful when those elements match. A lower price for another period or benefits is not demonstrated saving for equivalent protection.

Clarify payment arrangements and workforce changes. Do not treat another product's discount or tariff as an offer for your business. This article publishes no tariff, percentage saving or tax benefit. Tax treatment must be checked separately for the company.

Prepare simple employee instructions

Give included people a short explanation: insurer, period, how to verify inclusion and where to ask after an accident. Do not merely send a long document without the appropriate contact. Each employee should distinguish an information step from confirmation that a request is accepted.

In an emergency, medical help and safety come first. Contractual notification and documentation follow, with relevant records retained. Do not invent one deadline for all policies. The broker may explain administration but does not decide the benefit payment instead of the insurer.

An example for a workshop with mixed roles

A hypothetical workshop has production staff, administrative employees and a delivery driver. HR describes those activities and shift schedules separately. Management then checks which people and hours the proposal would include, rather than treating every position as office work.

When seasonal colleagues join, the company follows the update procedure confirmed in the contract. This example shows file organisation, not a real customer or compensated event. It does not demonstrate acceptance of a particular workshop by an insurer.

Check understanding before internal communication

Ask HR to explain three things in their own words: who is included, during which interval and where an event is reported. Compare the explanation with documents. If management and staff give different answers, correct communication before distributing an internal benefits presentation.

Keep an assessed proposal distinct from an active contract. A submitted request, completed list or broker conversation alone does not confirm protection has started. Obtain the document and applicable date, then inform people through the appropriate internal channel.

At renewal, check whether the original purpose still fits the team: are there new occupations, shifts or journeys? Update the description, not only the headcount. This avoids comparing an old package against changed activities while assuming conditions remain identical from year to year.

Also distinguish the company contact from the recipient of any benefit. An administrative role forwarding documents does not establish who receives payment. That identity must be checked in the proposed contract's conditions and documents.

A useful list for the first assessment

  • Headcount and actual activities by occupation group.
  • Hours, premises, travel and requested duration.
  • Benefits and amounts to compare.
  • Procedure for new employees and role changes.
  • Existing conditions if an active package is being checked.

Frequently asked questions about employee accidents

Is every employee automatically included in a group policy?

Do not assume so. Check the accepted list or inclusion mechanism, product criteria and when changes apply. Payroll headcounts do not replace confirmation of insured people.

Does accident insurance pay for every sickness absence?

No. The cause, event and product benefit must be assessed. A medical certificate alone does not establish entitlement under every contract. Ask for the proposed option's documents and assessment method.

Can the company choose the same amount for everyone?

It can request assessment of that structure, but acceptance and conditions require insurer confirmation. Present actual occupations and hours without hiding differences to simplify the presentation.

Does insurance remove workplace safety responsibilities?

Do not present it that way. Prevention, work organisation and legal duties need separate assessment. The policy concerns accepted contractual protection. Conclusions about an actual event's liability require specialist review.
